summary: Asked, for the first time, whether mypintusan's schedules, holiday calendar and site timezone survive contact with a running appliance (tools/fleetbench/bench_pintusan_schedules.py, 29 checks over 8 episodes; item 4 of the hardening register for the app that physically opens doors, after Secure Channel, the six alarms and offline mode). Decide()'s GATE 8 is the only gate whose answer changes with nobody touching the system, and every part of it is site-local: Snapshot.Location exists because a night shift that runs 22:00-06:00 and a public holiday are both wrong if evaluated in UTC. Its unit tests are good and all of them BUILD the snapshot they check, which is exactly the shape that lulls - scheduleAllows can be flawless while the window an operator types, the zone the site runs in, or the site a holiday is scoped to never reaches it. HOW THE CLOCK IS DRIVEN: a bench cannot wait until 02:00 to ask whether 02:00 is inside a night-shift window, and it does not have to - IANA zones span 26 hours of offset, so for any instant there is a real fixed-offset zone in which the wall clock is already at any hour you want, and each episode boots the appliance into one. That is not a simulation of the night shift, it is the night shift, somewhere. FOUR DEFECTS. (1) THE ONE WAY GATE 8 COULD FAIL OPEN. A window whose end equals its start fell into the wrapping (overnight) branch, where 'after the start' is true from the first minute of the day and the previous day's tail catches the rest - so a 09:00-09:00 window matched every hour of every day, on all seven weekdays, while the schedules screen labelled it '(overnight)'. Measured live: such a schedule opened a door at 02:51 that was meant to be shut until 09:00. The way in is not a typo on a form: Go's decoder drops unknown fields silently, so a client sending field names the API does not read has every window arrive as 0-0 while the 'a schedule needs at least one window' guard happily passes - which is precisely what four of this app's own bench scripts did (they posted startMinute/endMinute; the API reads startMin/endMin), so #211, #219, #220 and #221 all ran their whole lives on an accidental 24/7 schedule they believed was office hours. POST /api/schedules now refuses a zero-length window with a message naming the 24/7 flag, refuses a window starting at 24:00, and windowCovers treats a stored zero-length window as covering NOTHING so rows already written on an install cannot open a door; the four bench scripts now say always: true, which is what they meant. (2) CORRECTING THE SITE TIMEZONE DID NOT REACH THE RUNNING CONTROLLER. It is the FIRST thing the setup wizard asks for ('tell us where this site is, so opening hours and holidays are right'), on a controller that is already running, and it was read once at boot - so every fresh install evaluated its schedules and its holiday calendar in whatever zone config.json seeded, which on an appliance is UTC, until somebody power-cycled it. Measured live: with the site corrected to a zone where it was 12:22, a 09:00-17:00 grant went on being refused out-of-schedule because the controller was still deciding at 03:22. ControllerConfig.Location became func() *time.Location, asked freshly on every badge and backed by an atomic pointer on the runtime; runtime.ApplySettings swaps it on a settings save and REFUSES a zone that will not load rather than silently falling back to UTC. The bus list, the reader keys and the tick remain boot-only - re-reading those means tearing down every segment on the site - and the Settings screen's restart note (en/ms/zh/ar) was reworded to name only those. (3) A HOLIDAY COULD NOT BE SCOPED TO A SITE, BECAUSE NO DOOR COULD BE AT ONE. HolidayOn prefers a row matching the door's SiteId over a global one - the entire reason Holiday is its own entity, since Malaysian public holidays vary BY STATE - and store_sql_test.go tests that precedence with SiteId 5. No request shape ever carried a site onto a door, so every door on every install was at site 0, the site branch could never match, and a site-scoped holiday closed nothing anywhere. siteId is now accepted on POST /api/doors (0 still means 'follow the global calendar', right for the single-site appliance this mostly ships as); same shape as the offline policy fields before it, and it matters for the same reason - there is no PUT /api/doors, so a door keeps whatever placement it was born with. (4) NOTHING RECORDED WHO CHANGED THE CALENDAR. Creating or deleting a holiday is the one rule change that closes - or REOPENS - every door on a site for a whole day without anybody editing a grant, and it was the only access-rule mutation that published no access.rule-change notification; creating a schedule was missing one too. Both now publish, with the schedule's hours rendered into the audit line so a mistake is visible in it. ALSO ADDED: the holiday calendar had an API, a decision gate, a denial reason translated into four languages and client functions in lib/access.js - and NO SCREEN. Nothing in the app ever called listHolidays, createHoliday or deleteHoliday, so the calendar was empty on every install and the branch of scheduleAllows that reads it could not run. Access.js gained a Holidays section (admin-only, deny by default because that is what a public holiday means and it is the fail-closed answer, date entered as a calendar day in the site's zone, removal confirmed because it reopens a building), translated in en/ms/zh/ar. PROVEN GOOD and recorded as such, so it is not re-benched: the night shift works from BOTH sides (22:00-06:00 grants at 23:21 on its own weekday and still grants at 03:22 the next morning, and the wrapped tail correctly does NOT cover the day the window opened); the same rule at the same instant grants at a site where it is 12:22 and denies where it is 03:22, so the timezone genuinely decides; all three holiday behaviours work (deny closes and says holiday, ignore leaves the day ordinary, follow-sunday runs the Sunday timetable - checked in both directions, with a schedule that has no Sunday window and with one that has only a Sunday window); deleting a holiday reopens the door; and a holiday is resolved on the SITE's calendar date, not the server's, verified at a site whose local date was a day ahead of UTC. 29/29 checks pass with the fixes; 22/29 against the unfixed app.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no schema change. One new optional field on POST /api/doors (siteId, default 0 = follow the global holiday calendar), so an existing automation or the first-run wizard needs no change. ControllerConfig.Location changed from *time.Location to func() *time.Location - an internal Go type with one production caller (apps/mypintusan/app/runtime.go), no API or config surface. TWO BEHAVIOURAL CHANGES AN OPERATOR WILL NOTICE. First, POST /api/schedules now REFUSES a window whose end equals its start (400, with a message pointing at the 24/7 flag) where it used to accept one and grant round the clock. Any existing integration that sent zero-length windows - or, far likelier, sent window fields under names this API does not read, which produces the same 0-0 row - will now get an explicit error instead of silent 24/7 access; that is the point of the change. Existing zero-length rows already in a database are NOT migrated or deleted: they simply stop matching, so a schedule that was accidentally opening a door around the clock now denies out-of-schedule. On a site that entered such a window believing it meant 24/7, holders through that schedule will be refused until it is re-entered as a real window or the schedule is marked 24/7 - the safe direction, and the only correct one for a product with no fail-open policy anywhere else. Second, a site timezone edit (Settings screen, the settings API, or the first-run wizard's first step) now takes effect on the very next badge instead of at the next restart. A site that has been running with a wrong-but-restarted-into timezone sees no change; a site that saved a correction and never restarted will find its schedules and holidays move to the zone it asked for, which is what it asked for. Scope is `infra` rather than `mypintusan`: mypintusan has no entry in infra/versioning/version.json's apps map yet, and an unknown scope token hard-fails the release run.
